answer: For a poll on an island wharf on the river, two registrars each check an applicant's photo ID against the roll and their own issuance log. Each signs the poll-bound roll entry only for a match not already signed; otherwise they refuse. The server counts a ballot only with both signatures on the same entry, rejecting invalid or repeated entries. Assuming honest checks, extra ballots require more eligible people, potentially costing recruitment effort. Colluding registrars or borrowed IDs can defeat the check.
